notes: Second full sweep at db91c23: five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript comes from that model. No transcript has a Skill tool call or SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. All five added tests.

Verified in scratch copies of each project after mix deps.get: mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict and mix test pass in all five (17, 16, 15, 15 and 14 tests). Behaviour was checked with mix run on a script: 2 x APPLE at 100 gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five (sonnet-1 returns {:ok, cents}); opus-1 and sonnet-1 reject a second code, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 replace it; removing 5 of 2 units empties the items; BOGUS gives {:error, :unknown_code} in all five. Opus-1 and both Haiku runs trim and upcase the code; both Sonnet runs match it exactly. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError in four runs (documented in each @doc) and returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}} in sonnet-1.

Changed rule, now in the case's list and graded per run: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "Count the `<-` clauses before writing `with`. With one there is nothing to chain, and a `with` makes the reader look for the other steps, so use `case`, which shows both outcomes in one place." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, the rule's first paragraph and the paragraph after its first example). Violating runs out of 5: one-step with 1 (sonnet-1 lines 56 and 76; line 56 is the SKILL.md example's own apply-code shape); case nested in a with body 0; else 0. The other four write no with and are graded "not exercised", as instructed for this sweep. The check batch graded a no-with run "clean" when it handled a single fallible call with case; here that reading would change only opus-1 (case on parse_code/1 at lines 65-68), since the Haiku runs test membership with if and sonnet-2 uses function clauses. In the previous sweep 3 of 5 baseline runs had a one-step with (opus-1 line 51, sonnet-1 line 82, sonnet-2 line 69), not graded then because the rule was not in the case's list.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming (fetch sentence: "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`."; variable sentence: "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name."). Neither added sentence decides a verdict here. Violating runs per sentence, out of 5: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0; boolean functions end in ? 0 (no run defines one); get/fetch 0 (no run defines one; sonnet-1's subtotal_cents/2, which looks prices up and returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}}, is named by its job); size/length 0 (not exercised); ignored values 0; domain variable names 0. acc, current and normalized are held to the earlier standard, which passed them.

Before you finish (unchanged text): clean in 1 of 5. Opus-1 ran format, compile --warnings-as-errors, test and credo --strict in one chain after its last edit. Haiku-1 ran only mix test and mix format --check-formatted; haiku-2 added mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force but never ran Credo; both Sonnet runs ran only mix format && mix test, as in the previous sweep. Refused commands: haiku-1 had two (an exploratory xargs sh -c, and a mix test / format-check chain with echo "exit $?", which it re-ran as two commands), haiku-2 one (the same exploratory xargs), sonnet-2 one (a python3 heredoc edit that also carried mix format && mix test, which it re-ran after writing the files with Write and Edit). Sonnet-1 issued one tool call named bash_placeholder with empty input, which failed as an unknown tool; it was not a permission refusal. No refused command carried Credo or the compiler, so the verdicts stand.

other_violations follows the previous grades. Sums written with Enum.reduce where Enum.sum_by/2 fits are listed under the Enum/Map rule, whose sum row is unchanged (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2; sonnet-1 halts on a missing price with reduce_while, which sum_by cannot do). Multi-step pipelines written on one line, and sonnet-1's single-step pipe in a test, are listed under the pipeline rule, as the previous skill grades and the check batch listed them; the previous baseline grade did not list the same `case code |> String.trim() |> String.upcase() do` line in its opus-1 and sonnet-1, so baseline counts for that rule are not comparable across the two sweeps. Not listed: pipelines that start with Cart.new(), because the project's own test file starts its pipelines that way (SKILL.md, "Existing projects"), and @doc without ## Examples, because the project's existing @docs have none, as in the previous grades for this case.
Expected reads (testing.md when the run adds or changes tests) applies to skill runs. All five baseline runs added tests and read no skill file, as the baseline prompt requires.
